concepts.title: Arithmetic Mean (Ungrouped Data)
concepts.definition: The arithmetic mean is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations, giving a single representative value of the data set.
concepts.key_idea: The mean balances the data so that the total of deviations above and below it cancel out.
question_patterns: calculate the arithmetic mean of the given ungrouped data
find the mean of the following observations
compute the average of the data set provided
determine the mean income from the list of values
calculate the mean marks obtained by students

solution_steps.action: Sum all observations in the data set
solution_steps.explain: Add every individual value x_i together to get the total sum.

solution_steps.action: Count the number of observations
solution_steps.explain: Determine n, the total count of data points in the set.

solution_steps.action: Divide the total by the count
solution_steps.explain: Divide the sum of observations by the number of observations to obtain the mean.

worked_examples.question: Find the mean of the data: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Sum = 10 + 20 + 30 + 40 + 50 = 150. Step 2: Number of observations n = 5. Step 3: Mean = 150 / 5 = 30.

worked_examples.question: The daily wages of 5 workers are Rs 100, Rs 150, Rs 200, Rs 250, Rs 300. Calculate the mean wage.

exercises.question: Calculate the mean of the following data: 5, 15, 25, 35, 45.
The marks of 6 students are 48, 56, 72, 64, 80, 60. Find the mean mark.

concepts.title: Median (Ungrouped Data)
concepts.definition: The median is the middle value of an ordered data set that divides the observations into two equal halves, with half the values below and half above it.
concepts.formula: median = middle value (odd n) or average of two middle values (even n)
concepts.key_idea: The median is unaffected by extreme values and is found after arranging data in ascending or descending order.
question_patterns: find the median of the given ungrouped data
determine the middle value of the ordered data set
calculate the median for an even number of observations
compute the median income from the given list
find the median marks of the students

solution_steps.action: Arrange the data in ascending order
solution_steps.explain: Sort all observations from smallest to largest so the middle position can be located.

solution_steps.action: Determine the position of the median
solution_steps.explain: If n is odd, the median is at position (n+1)/2. If n is even, the median is the average of values at positions n/2 and (n/2)+1.

solution_steps.action: Extract or average the middle value(s)
solution_steps.explain: For odd n take the single middle value; for even n take the average of the two central values.

worked_examples.question: Find the median of: 25, 10, 40, 15, 30.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Sorted data = 10, 15, 25, 30, 40. Step 2: n = 5 (odd), median position = (5+1)/2 = 3rd value. Step 3: Median = 25.

worked_examples.question: Find the median of: 8, 3, 15, 12, 20, 7.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Sorted data = 3, 7, 8, 12, 15, 20. Step 2: n = 6 (even), median is average of 3rd and 4th values. Step 3: Median = (8 + 12) / 2 = 10.

exercises.question: The ages of 7 people are 12, 18, 25, 30, 40, 55, 70. Find the median age.

concepts.title: Mode (Ungrouped Data)
concepts.definition: The mode is the value that occurs most frequently in a data set, representing the observation with the highest frequency.
concepts.key_idea: A data set may be unimodal (one mode), bimodal (two modes), or have no mode if all values occur equally.
question_patterns: find the mode of the given ungrouped data
identify the most frequent value in the data set
determine the mode of the following observations
calculate the modal value of the data
find the mode and state if the data is unimodal or bimodal

solution_steps.action: Count the frequency of each value in the data set
solution_steps.explain: Tally how many times each distinct value appears in the observations.

solution_steps.action: Identify the maximum frequency
solution_steps.explain: Find the highest count among all the value frequencies.

solution_steps.action: Select the value(s) with the maximum frequency
solution_steps.explain: The value with the highest frequency is the mode; if multiple values share the highest frequency, the data is multimodal.

worked_examples.question: Find the mode of: 5, 7, 7, 8, 5, 7, 9, 5, 7.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Frequencies: 5 appears 3 times, 7 appears 4 times, 8 appears once, 9 appears once. Step 2: Maximum frequency = 4. Step 3: Mode = 7 (appears 4 times).

worked_examples.question: Find the mode of: 2, 4, 4, 6, 6, 8.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Frequencies: 2 appears once, 4 appears twice, 6 appears twice, 8 appears once. Step 2: Maximum frequency = 2. Step 3: Modes = 4 and 6 (bimodal).

exercises.question: Determine whether the data 3, 5, 5, 7, 9 has a mode. Justify.

concepts.title: Range as a Measure of Dispersion
concepts.definition: Range is the simplest measure of dispersion, defined as the difference between the largest and smallest observations in a data set.
concepts.key_idea: Range gives a quick sense of the spread of data but is highly sensitive to extreme values.
question_patterns: calculate the range of the given data
find the spread of the data set using range
determine the range of the following observations
compute the range and interpret the dispersion
compare the range of two data sets

solution_steps.action: Identify the maximum value in the data set
solution_steps.explain: Find the largest observation among all the data points.

solution_steps.action: Identify the minimum value in the data set
solution_steps.explain: Find the smallest observation among all the data points.

solution_steps.action: Subtract the minimum from the maximum
solution_steps.explain: The difference between the largest and smallest value gives the range.

worked_examples.question: Find the range of: 12, 45, 8, 33, 27, 50.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Maximum value = 50. Step 2: Minimum value = 8. Step 3: Range = 50 - 8 = 42.

worked_examples.question: The daily temperatures of a week are 30, 32, 28, 35, 31, 29, 34 degrees C. Find the range.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Maximum temperature = 35. Step 2: Minimum temperature = 28. Step 3: Range = 35 - 28 = 7 degrees C.

exercises.question: Two data sets have ranges 15 and 50. Which is more dispersed and why?

concepts.title: Standard Deviation (Ungrouped Data)
concepts.definition: Standard deviation is the positive square root of the average of the squared deviations of each observation from the mean, measuring the absolute dispersion of data around the mean.
concepts.key_idea: A lower standard deviation indicates data points are close to the mean, while a higher value indicates greater spread.
question_patterns: calculate the standard deviation of the given data
find the standard deviation for ungrouped observations
compute the standard deviation and interpret the result
determine the dispersion using standard deviation
compare the standard deviation of two data sets

solution_steps.action: Calculate the mean of the data
solution_steps.explain: Find the arithmetic mean which serves as the reference point for deviations.

solution_steps.action: Compute the sum of squared deviations from the mean
solution_steps.explain: For each observation, subtract the mean and square the result, then add all squared deviations.

solution_steps.action: Divide by n and take the square root
solution_steps.explain: Divide the sum of squared deviations by the number of observations and take the positive square root to get the standard deviation.

exercises.question: Two data sets have standard deviations 2 and 8. Which is more consistent and why?

concepts.title: Variance (Ungrouped Data)
concepts.definition: Variance is the average of the squared deviations of each observation from the mean, and is the square of the standard deviation.
concepts.key_idea: Variance measures the average squared spread of data; it is always non-negative and its unit is the square of the original unit.
question_patterns: calculate the variance of the given data
find the variance for ungrouped observations
compute the variance and relate it to standard deviation
determine the variance of the data set
calculate variance and interpret the dispersion

solution_steps.action: Calculate the mean of the data
solution_steps.explain: Find the arithmetic mean as the reference for measuring deviations.

solution_steps.action: Compute the sum of squared deviations from the mean
solution_steps.explain: Subtract the mean from each observation, square each difference, and sum them all.

solution_steps.action: Divide the sum of squared deviations by n
solution_steps.explain: Dividing by the number of observations gives the average squared deviation, which is the variance.

exercises.question: If the standard deviation of a data set is 5, what is its variance?

concepts.title: Index Numbers: Introduction, WPI and CPI
concepts.definition: An index number is a statistical device measuring the relative change in a variable over time with the base period set to 100; the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) tracks wholesale-level price changes while the Consumer Price Index (CPI) tracks retail price changes paid by consumers for a basket of goods and services.
concepts.formula: index_number = (value in current period / value in base period) * 100; CPI = (sum of current retail prices / sum of base retail prices) * 100
concepts.key_idea: Index numbers express changes as percentages relative to a base period; WPI reflects producer-level prices for policy while CPI reflects the cost of living for consumers and is used to adjust wages and pensions.
question_patterns: what is an index number and how is it constructed
calculate the index number for the given price data
distinguish between Wholesale Price Index and Consumer Price Index
explain the construction and uses of the Consumer Price Index
calculate the CPI for the given basket of goods

solution_steps.action: Identify the basket prices in the base period and the current period
solution_steps.explain: Collect the base period and current period prices for each item in the consumer or wholesale basket.

solution_steps.action: Compute the ratio of current period total to base period total
solution_steps.explain: Divide the sum of current prices by the sum of base prices to find the relative price change.

solution_steps.action: Multiply the ratio by 100 to obtain the index number
solution_steps.explain: Converting the ratio to a percentage index with base = 100 gives the WPI or CPI.

worked_examples.question: The price of a commodity was Rs 50 in 2010 (base year) and Rs 75 in 2020. Calculate the price index.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Base value = 50, current value = 75. Step 2: Ratio = 75/50 = 1.5. Step 3: Index number = 1.5 * 100 = 150.

worked_examples.question: A consumer basket has base year cost Rs 1000 and current year cost Rs 1200. Calculate the CPI.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Base total = 1000, current total = 1200. Step 2: Ratio = 1200/1000 = 1.2. Step 3: CPI = 1.2 * 100 = 120.

worked_examples.question: The wholesale price total of a basket was Rs 500 in the base year and Rs 650 in the current year. Find the WPI.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Base total = 500, current total = 650. Step 2: Ratio = 650/500 = 1.3. Step 3: WPI = 1.3 * 100 = 130.

exercises.question: Distinguish between WPI and CPI in terms of purpose and coverage.
A basket costs Rs 800 in the base year and Rs 960 in the current year. Calculate the CPI.
Explain why the base period is always assigned an index value of 100.

concepts.title: Inflation and Uses of Index Numbers
concepts.definition: Inflation is the sustained rise in the general price level over time, measured as the percentage rate of change in a price index such as the CPI or WPI; index numbers are widely used to measure this change, determine purchasing power, deflate monetary values, and guide economic policy and wage adjustments.
concepts.key_idea: Index numbers are essential for measuring inflation, which erodes purchasing power; they also help compare economic variables over time, adjust incomes for inflation, and formulate government fiscal and monetary policies.
question_patterns: calculate the inflation rate from the given index numbers
explain how index numbers are used to measure inflation
describe the uses of index numbers in economics
how do index numbers help in policy formulation and wage adjustment
discuss the importance of index numbers in deflating monetary values

solution_steps.action: Identify the price index for the current period and the previous (base) period
solution_steps.explain: Obtain the CPI or WPI values for the two periods being compared.

solution_steps.action: Find the difference between the current and previous index
solution_steps.explain: Subtract the previous period index from the current period index to find the absolute change.

solution_steps.action: Divide the difference by the previous index and multiply by 100
solution_steps.explain: Express the change as a percentage of the previous period index to get the inflation rate.

worked_examples.question: The CPI in 2020 was 150 and in 2021 it was 165. Calculate the inflation rate.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Current index = 165, previous index = 150. Step 2: Difference = 165 - 150 = 15. Step 3: Inflation rate = (15/150) * 100 = 10%.

worked_examples.question: How is the Consumer Price Index used to adjust dearness allowance for workers?
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: The CPI measures the change in the cost of a consumer basket. Step 2: A rise in CPI indicates an increase in the cost of living. Step 3: Wages and dearness allowance are adjusted upward in proportion to the CPI increase to maintain real income.
worked_examples.answer: CPI is used to adjust dearness allowance so that real wages keep pace with the rising cost of living

worked_examples.question: If the WPI rises from 200 to 220, find the rate of inflation.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Current index = 220, previous index = 200. Step 2: Difference = 220 - 200 = 20. Step 3: Inflation rate = (20/200) * 100 = 10%.

exercises.question: The CPI was 180 in 2021 and 198 in 2022. Calculate the inflation rate.
List any four important uses of index numbers in economics.
Explain how index numbers help in deflating nominal income to real income.
